name: Dai Yem Waterfall
kicker: Two limestone drops you hear before you see
summary: Walk down to two limestone drops at Ban Vat, the fall you hear before you see. A pool sits under the lower water, and a red glass bridge crosses above the falls. The drop is given as over 100 m, and the first fall is also given as about 70 m. The provincial recognition gives no tariff. Skip it when the tea rows are the only morning you wanted.
getThere: From the farm town on National Highway 43. The two route descriptions disagree.
heroCaption: The wide falls, the limestone, and the pool under the lower water

notice.title: The published heights do not agree
notice.body: The drop is given as over 100 m. The first fall is also given as about 70 m, in three tiers. Do not treat those as one number. The fee is check on arrival.

body: Walk down to the limestone falls at Ban Vat. The water comes in two parts, with a pool under the lower drop. You hear it before you see it. A red glass bridge crosses above the falls. An older description of the stair paths does not mention that bridge. The bridge is the later feature.

Keep both heights. The drop is given as over 100 m. The first fall is also given as about 70 m and in three tiers, with a first tier about 40 m deep, about 70 m wide, and about 50 m high, and the two falls are put about 200 m apart. They are also put 150 m apart, with a sheet about 70 m wide when the water is full.

The fullest water is given as April to September. The first fall’s lip is also given as May to September, and the second fall as April to September. The 18 Jan 2022 provincial recognition names the site and gives no tariff. The fee, the hours, and how long you stay are check on arrival.

figures.caption: The lip and the sheet, from under the fall
figures.alt: White water leaving a dark rock lip at Dai Yem, with forest on both sides

gettingThere: The falls are at Bản Vặt, xã Mường Sang, on National Highway 43. A 2022 provincial row still uses that address. Ward names after 2025 are check on arrival.

One drive, toward Son La, is about 3 km on National Highway 6 to the Long Sap junction, then left about 5 km on National Highway 43. Toward Hanoi, the same description gives about 1 km to that junction, then right about 5 km. Another description says 3 km from the farm town, and also about 4 km from the Pa Hang junction. The two descriptions do not match. Minutes are check on arrival.

closed: No weekly closing day is given. Check on arrival.
